subject: FinServCo — Redwood evals setup & recommended models
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finservco.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: FinServCo — Redwood evals setup & recommended models

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can get the customer-specific evals running on Redwood: 

1) Goal: validate model fit for FinServCo workflows (customer support summarization + answer retrieval) and measure quality regressions vs your current baseline.

2) Recommended models to include in the initial run (we'll expand after the first pass):
   - redwood-instruct-13b (dense, strong instruction-following)
   - redwood-7b-rl (good latency/cost tradeoff for short responses)
   - redwood-3b-v1 (fast, cost-efficient baseline)

3) Eval types & metrics (suggested):
   - Generation quality: ROUGE-L, BLEU for summaries; exact-match / F1 for retrieval answers.
   - Hallucination check: automated reference comparison + 50 human-eval samples for precision.
   - Latency & token cost: P50/P95 per model for your average prompt length.

4) Dataset format (attached template):
   - CSV with columns: id, prompt, reference, intent, metadata_json
   - Prefer UTF-8; prompts separated by "\n\n" where needed; include estimated token_count column if available.

5) Scoring criteria (attached guidelines):
   - Automatic: ROUGE-L / BLEU / EM / F1 depending on task.
   - Human: 1-5 Likert for relevance/faithfulness, binary hallucination flag.

6) Next steps / asks from FinServCo:
   - Share a QA/summary sample dataset (min 500 rows, stratified by intent) using the attached template.
   - Create a temporary project/workspace in Redwood and grant marissa.cole@redwood.com and neha.kapoor@redwood.com access (we can also set up a one-off API key).
   - Book a 1-hour SE session to onboard the dataset + run the first eval (Vivek recommended Mon/Tue next week).

Attachments: eval_dataset_template.csv, sample_prompt_set.json, scoring_guidelines.md

I've attached a lightweight prompt set example and the dataset template to speed things up. Once we have the CSV, Neha/Vivek will run the first pass and share the dashboard + a benchmark XLSX for your team.

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0124

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks — we'll take the S3 export once it's ready. A few technical details to make the first run smooth: 

- File requirements: CSV UTF-8, header row present. Please avoid embedded newlines in the reference column; if needed, wrap in quotes.
- Tokenization: we'll use the redwood token encoder; if you can provide a rough token_count column that helps us choose truncation thresholds.
- Sampling: please ensure the 800-row export is stratified by intent and includes ~50 examples from low-frequency intents for edge-case coverage.
- Max prompt + reference length: we recommend <= 2,048 tokens for the initial pass; if you have longer contexts we can test a second pass with KV-cache enabled.

Scoring plan (what we'll run on Redwood):
- Automated: ROUGE-L for summarization; EM/F1 for retrieval QA. We'll produce per-intent and per-model sheets in the benchmark workbook.
- Human eval: we'll surface 50 failure candidates per model (low automatic score) for a short human review run using the attached scoring_guidelines.md template.

Operational notes: 
- We'll create a temporary project named "FinServCo-Evals-RDW-4873" and invite marissa.cole@redwood.com and neha.kapoor@redwood.com; Alex/Priya, once you accept, you'll see the eval dashboard at: https://redwood-internal.com/evals/RDW-2027-4873
- After the initial run we'll share a bench_results.xlsx with per-model P50/P95 latency, token costs, and quality metrics.

Scheduling: Marissa, Vivek — Tue 29th 11am ET is open on my calendar for the SE session; Alex/Priya please confirm.

Shortlist of deliverables after the SE session:
1) First-pass benchmark dashboard link
2) bench_results.xlsx (auto-generated)
3) 50 human-eval judgments and a summary hallucination rate
4) Recommendations for model + quantization profile for production (cost/latency trade-offs)

Let me know if you'd like tweaks to the scoring rules before we run.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
